keys.beat: Penelope orders Eurycleia to move the marriage bed outside the chamber for the stranger.
keys.text: 'Make his bed for him outside the room that he himself built. Bring the bed outside this room, and put bedding upon it with fleeces, good coverlets, and blankets.' She said this in order to try him.

keys.beat: Odysseus erupts, explaining that he built the bed around a living olive tree and no one could move it intact.
keys.text: 'There was a young olive growing within the precincts of the house... I built my room round this with strong walls of stone... then I cut off the top boughs of the olive tree and left the stump standing. This I dressed roughly from the root upwards and then worked with carpenter's tools well and skilfully.'

keys.beat: The secret proves identity; Penelope runs to him and embraces him.
keys.text: When she heard the sure proofs Ulysses now gave her, she fairly broke down. She flew weeping to his side, flung her arms about his neck, and kissed him.

keys.beat: She explains that fear of deception caused her delay.
keys.text: 'Do not be angry with me, Ulysses... I have been shuddering all the time through fear that someone might come here and deceive me with a lying story.'

keys.beat: Athena holds back dawn while husband and wife weep and reunite.
keys.text: Minerva... made the night long, and held back Dawn in her golden throne on the Oceanus, nor would she let her yoke her fleet horses Lampus and Phaethon that bear light to men.
